claims.claim: Reviewers report that starting new worlds causes game crashes or entire operating system crashes.

citations.review_text:
Dwarf Fortress has been out for 20 years. For three quarters of those twenty years, I have been playing Dwarf Fortress. Not consistently, sometimes going years on without playing it, but I've been there. I have a lot of opinions from thousands of hours of gameplay, and I've bought the game four times now, thrice sending money directly to Bay 12 as a donation. I'm proudly on the wall of champions, and I don't regret that purchase.

Here's the TL;DR. Dwarf Fortress is a massive game with a glacial development speed, questionable design choices, and it is not for everyone at such a core level that you might not even understand if it is for you or not after hundreds of hours of gameplay. It's more of a personal belief than a real true or false statement. But it is for me, or maybe it was, and I just haven't realized I've moved on from it yet.

Alright, so here's the thing. Dwarf Fortress has changed massively in these last twenty years, and I can't deny it, but I also can't say that I agree with every single change made. I can't say that I agree with some older changes, and also some newer changes. Things like removing keyboard controls, or focusing on graphics over enhancing the gameplay as things continue to be worked on. I can't agree with how difficult modding has become with the changes to visuals. I don't even know if I agree with the new music, but I'll say that I am just being curmudgeonly on that regard, and resistant to change. 

Some of the artwork that's come out of the game is just downright atrocious, and I understand that it's just some artist's style, but there really should be some revisions done on a few of the animals and animal people. Some really got hit badly by the ugly stick. I understand that art is a major reason why development has slowed to an utter crawl even compared to before, but just throwing up the first pass and calling it done is a disservice to the game. Thankfully, mods exist, so it's a lesser issue. (EDIT: They may have done more p…

Game is literally unplayable, and it doesnt matter whether this (steam) or free version.
I came back to dwarf fortress after a few years of not playing. Every version from 50.04 upwards causes either CTD or whole OS crashes. I tried every solution - installing C++/MSVC redistributables, running game in windowed/fullscreen mode, turning multithreading, administrador mode, windows DPI optimization on and off, updating drivers, but to no avail. Game crashes after at most 5-10 minutes, whether playing with or without tutorial after starting new world.
Its a shame, especially considering i liked mouse support, new graphics and music a lot!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the controls and user interface as clunky, unintuitive, and difficult to use.

citations.review_text:
Am I the crazy one? I played it for a bit and cannot stand the UI and controls. I watched a bunch of reviews and wanted to like it, but this just isn't for me.

Maybe one day I'll come back and try it again, but if you don't like clunky controls, I cannot recommend this game.
Grade: D

Too overwhelming as a new player. Every menu / workshop has hundreds of items and you have no clue what their importance is. The UI and tooltips are unintuitive.

The tutorial barely tells you much at all. Subsequent help guides are fine, but events happen before you've even gotten your feet underneath you. So while I'm still working on figuring out gardening, the all-important trade caravan's already arrived signaling the coming of winter. Interacting with the trader, the total value of bought / sold items doesn't update, so I have no idea what my goods are actually worth and what I'm actually able to trade for.

This is a game for people who have loads of patience or don't mind watching YouTube videos to learn a game.

[h1]I would love to play this more, but my eyes bleed.[/h1]

Both [u]Songs of Syx[/u] and [u]Rimworld[/u] are beautifully crafted games that took a lot of inspiration from Dwarf Fortress - which is basically "the king" of all colony sims. And while graphics usually don't matter to me, the ASCII-based foundation of this game is just too much. With the release of this "premium" version I thought "well, now is finally the time," but no one told me it's just a reskin and the engine is basically the same. There are no animations, no smooth transitions, and the controls are clunky. You can't even move the camera smoothly because it is tied to a grid. The general awkwardness and the smell of "fossilized feces" in the game's systems made me quit very fast.

[i] Why do I need a simulation of eyelids for every character when I can't even see two characters clink their beers in a single tile? It is all text-based. Visually, they are just standing still in two separate tiles about 1 meter from each other without even a mug in their hands. Atp just remove graphics completely, and make it an interactive book.[/i] 

I know the game is great, but I don't think it should look like this in 2026. [b][u]It needs a full engine remake[/u][/b] rather than just an ASCII glyphs reskin, to look at least as good as the two games mentioned above(not speaking about all those beautiful other colony/city sims). It needs smooth animations, handheld items, nice lighting systems, and fancy interactions.

[h3]Game 9/10, Engine 1/10. Don't buy this if you were fooled by the screenshots like I was and thought "oh, so it's just Rimworld but better."[/h3]

So technically this game came first, but it's a more buggy less visually refined version of Rimworld I'd argue. 
I've tried to play this game multiple times, and was left confused most of the time. At first, I thought I was just regarded, but you start playing it and realize some things are just broken. 
Going through the tutorial, which I couldn't finish, I found several bugs with just trying to explain the game. One of them that comes to mind is how it completely skipped a step regarding mining out a room. Not a big deal really, I figured out how the staircase works. However, when I selected for it to go two levels deep, I left it alone and just let the person dig. I was reading the tutorial, and when I went to go back to check, it was dug probably 12 levels deep. 
Obviously not what I wanted it to do. I had no idea how to stop or even deconstruct the stairs, so I just decided to restart with a new world and retry to tutorial. After having them dig, and do it right, I realized that the previous tutorial glitched and just skipped a few steps like stockpiling and stuff. Pretty annoying as I couldn't have accidentally skipped them due to the tutorial being task based. Though whatever, bugs happen. But when I went to build another staircase probably 10 tiles east, nobody moved to actually do the work. Thought that was weird, and decided to just make the new staircase a block away to see if it was another bug. It was not, they just didn't want to build that staircase for reasons I couldn't figure out. Moved on, once again slightly annoyed.
I got to the woodcutting part. Tried to cut down a tree while at level 0, or whatever ground level is called, put in the task only to see no visual changes. Figured it was just something tasked and didn't have a visual indicator. I scrolled up, and found that only a branch of the tree was designated as cut, but it was too high off the ground to be reached. Tried to just cut the main tree, and again, same problem. Tried a few more unt…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks full keyboard-only support and that old keyboard controls are missing from the current version.

citations.review_text:
Was happy to give my money to folks that made a great free game back in the day. Unfortunately this was the death of the game. Almost 4 years since Steam release and we are still missing the keyboard only support that we've had forever. Even the ASCII version offered in the current versions has been destroyed. 

Instead of polishing the game and aligning Classic/Steam versions so everyone is happy, we are given Dinosaurs. 

Save your money, download v0.47 from the website for free and Lazy Newb Pack to play with non-ASCII tilesets. 

Remember, this game is a free game. You're only paying for the graphic Sprites. Even if you want mouse support, I still don't recommend giving any more money to this Publisher and game. Their priorities are money, not the game itself. Polishing/Bug fixing (other than bugs they created in a previous patch) is not conducive to sales. Worthless content like Dinosaurs are because you get a nice little marketable Announcement.
I'll change the review the day they re-enable the old keyboard controls in full.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the in-game soundtrack, highlighting natural-sounding instruments, reverb, and vocal tracks in the dwarven language.

citations.review_text:
I can't fathom why I adore DF so much and bounce off Rimworld every time I try it.

It feels so much simpler and more straightforward despite being THE infamously complex autistic story generator game.

But the thing I didn't expect to like that much AT ALL is the atmosphere. It's not a very visual game, but nonetheless the style is very coherent between the game itself and the UI. But the thing that ties all of it together is THE MUSIC. OMG THE MUSIC.

Imagine my surprise when a silly dorf game turned out to have one of my favourite videogame soundtracks EVER. Last time I heard this good of a symbiosis between the game and the music was back when I played Roadwarden for the first time. The instruments sound natural, messy, with a very nice reverb that makes you feel like you're in a cave and this is what the dorfs might actually be playing. Most of the tracks have an air of melancholy that comes with routine work and the passage of time, some tracks include vocals sang in the dwarven language (just listen to Drink & Industry, it's simply the best tavern theme ever recorded in my opinion), a lot of tracks also include background sounds like birds chirping, crickets trilling or thunder roaring, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ it's just PERFECT. For the kind of game Dwarf Fortress is, the soundtrack had to be done JUST RIGHT. There are barely any visuals, animations, anything at all really. Iirc Tarn and Zach always envisioned DF to be a simulation of a fantasy world, but before the Steam release the player had to do a lot of work to make it feel alive for themselves. This music changes that, without substituting for imagination. It attaches pictures to words. What a magnificent ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ job.

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative) – [7/10] [/b] [/h1]
The game world is the star of the show and something truly special. I loved how vast the world is and how you can build your fortress underground, multilevel. It not only adds in lore accuracy for dwarves, but it’s (to my knowledge) one of the big things that successors, like Rimworld, lack. 

There is no set narrative here. Instead, you create your own stories through your colony. 

[h1][b] Gameplay (Mechanics/Difficulty) – [7/10] [/b] [/h1]
The mechanics are….vast, but unrefined. You’ll find depth intertwined within the lives of your colony. There actions, everything, can be micromanaged to an insane degree. The complexity is as intriguing here as it is a negative - I can understand how first-time players like myself might feel overwhelmed at best, and lost without a wiki page at worst. The game doesn’t explain much outside of its 20-minute tutorial. It basically teaches you how to designate zones, construct a bed, and….. good luck! 

The difficulty, at least with only 10 hours of gameplay, felt forgiving. You won’t be raided or shown combat at the start for the same reason the narrative is played on a macro level - the world doesn’t know about your existence. Instead, the primary difficulty of the game comes from its uninviting UI and the complexity that requires a wiki to understand.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game has a steep learning curve and is difficult to figure out without external guides or wikis.

citations.review_text: way too hard and complicated

So if you're coming to DF from Rimworld like I am, it might take you a little longer to get into it but you will have a great time. I am. You can definitely see the influence of the original DF (ASCII) on Rimworld though. 
There are is definitely a steep learning curve for balancing everything, but the actual game is pretty easy to pick up. I think the tutorial could go a little further. It relly should set you up with drink and food at the very least. That is the number one issues for me at the beginning. Grumpy little dwarves. 
While I prefer to the enormous amount of mods for Rimworld and the gameplay is better suited to my style because I've been playing it so long, I can easily see DF being a contender for screentime and it runs a lot better on my older linux machine than Rimworld, so it's nice to have it running in the background when i'm doing other things. 9/10

Its an alright colony sim with a lot of depth. Biggest problem is by far the most cumbersome UI i've tried using. Nothing makes any sense, nothing is intuitive and there is hardly any information about any of the things you are trying to do. Or about what you need to do.

To be honest. I'm probably gonna a lot of hate for this. But I find it unintuitive. I like rimworld. Unfair comparison? Maybe, yes. The point is, I can see it's a good game, but I can't seem to figure out how to actually play it properly. I've looked at tutorials which helped but it seems like I can't do the things I want to do in any obvious way without reading tutorials for half an hour. 

This is a middle review but for anyone like me, I honestly couldn't recommend it. But I can see why many people like it. Sorry.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the user interface and menus as cumbersome, confusing, and poorly designed.

citations.review_text: Pretty good oldschool colony sim, even though it has some rusty controls and UX solusiton. It's definitely more accessible for most of the players with those graphics instead of ASCII. It's kind of like the RimWorld, but on bigger scale and with many-many-many layers (floors) instead of just 1 floor. I thought it would be much harder to dig into it, but it was not so bad really, the tutorials are pretty much fine, although some stuff requires googling anyway (even with all the additional tutorials). Oh, and the sounds are very poor in this game – it's kinda ok without the sounds, but almost all the time the game feels muted or bugged in terms of sound.

Big fan of colony sims - the more complex the better. But I can't recommend this one. The UI and quality of life features in this game are horrible.. like punch me in the face horrible, The amount of duplicate configurations and layouts required to get your supply chains up and running is incredibly tedious. But maybe that's the appeal.. maybe all the overwhelming ratings are because people just love clicking through badly designed menus over and over again.

I genuinely feel like the only people who will truly enjoy this are people who played this years ago. It is overpriced, outdated (despite still being updates), clunky, and suffers from poor UI and QoL issues.

If you want a monumentally better game than this, I recommend Songs of Syx, with the main downside being that Dwarf Fortress lets you mine on different elevations (up/down), while Songs of Syx doesn't.
[hr][/hr]

This game has a horrendous UI, some of the worst QoL controls I've ever seen (You can place tons of structures in 1 click, but I couldn't find a way to cancel all of them so I had to manually click on each one and click the cancel button), the units move by tile hopping (no animation to go to next tile, just teleports), random sounds will play even while the game is paused like wolves howling and a sound that sounds like a cave-in, and plenty of more minor issues that just entirely put me off from even trying to build a fortress. 

I have 1800 games in my Steam library, and I am almost certain that this is the "scammiest" Colony Sim I currently own, considering its price. Its really a shame because I have literally only heard good things about this, but I'm assuming its a cult mentality or 30+ year olds who refuse to try any new games. :/

Its an alright colony sim with a lot of depth. Biggest problem is by far the most cumbersome UI i've tried using. Nothing makes any sense, nothing is intuitive and there is hardly any information about any of the things you are trying to do. Or about what you need to do.

A legendary game on the level of tetris and mario in terms of inspiring modern games. My two hours of playtime does not represent my experience here, I played hours and hours of the free classic version.

As far as this version goes, menuing in the classic version is pretty awful and has always been the main obstacle to enjoyment for many, and that's the main thing they're trying to add here. It still isn't perfect but it's an improvement. There have always been community mods for the classic version to add graphics and stuff, so much of the stuff that the steam version is doing isn't exactly new, but now Tarn and Zach have the millions of dollars they so richly deserve instead of living in poverty for decades while continuing to work on one of the most influential video games in all of history.

Why should you buy this? "This is our life's work and we're never going to stop." They've been doing it for 20 years at this point. They mean it when they say that.

You will have to open wiki or online disscussions to resolve every damn thing every 2 minutes because there is so little number of explanations ingame and it is extremely counterintuitive. Add a lot of bugs that still exist after 20 years of development or something (or 4 of steam I suppose). But its okay, it is developed by 2 people, if the game is good I do not care about QoL and all time I spent on trying to, for example, create ladder up from underground by trying 999 different things because it is impossible to just build ladder from underground. To be honest, it is impossible to "just do" anything in this game, but it could be managed, if you really want it.

But why to want it? Every time I tried to play DF, even 10 years ago, nothing ever happened in my fortress. Like maybe a couple of times i got "strange mood" effect on dwarfs, but that is basically it. Almost no events, nothing unique, many generic guests, but I never was even managed to find anything underground beyond ores. I suppose I can wait more than 10 hours for something to happen, mine 90 more layers, but it is the same thing every time, three times already - nothing is happening. 

Also, there is no other active maps other then your fortress. If you are sending soilders to attack anything on global map, everything happens behind curtains. claims.claim: Reviewers report that the Steam version lacks full keyboard support, forcing reliance on the mouse for basic actions and causing physical discomfort or strain during play sessions.

citations.review_text: I like the old terminal version more but this version is solid. i wish this game had options for doing things on keyboard since it used to be my go to laptop game back in high school/university like a decade ago but the newer mouse centric design is rough on a trackpad with this version. It's still the undefeatable best colony sim game out there nonetheless.

I've been waiting three and a half years for the promised full keyboard support. The UI is awful, with its worst areas comparable to the worst areas of pre-steam DF except now you *have* to use a mouse and can't even do basic things anymore like scroll with arrow keys or the page keys or even fuzzy search. Playing Steam DF for more than 30 minutes at a time causes an RSI flare-up that no other game I have ever played has, including other colony sims like Rimworld and Songs of Syx.

So many little things are just gone. Health screen, wound overview, civilian alerts (technically not but you need DFHack to access them). Not to even mention the bugs, some of which were years old pre-Steam. Its a shame because the performance improvements, worldgen speed, and the siege update are awesome.

A proper re-introduction of keyboard support has been a "top priority" and "in the works" and "coming soon" for literal YEARS, and now the new cope is "lua support might let DFHack fix it, maybe I guess". 

And no, the free version does not fix this. That is just the Steam version set to ASCII mode and still has the exact same UI.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that adventure mode lacks certain features, such as healing, standard skill usage, or cooking mechanics, and requires mods to play effectively.

citations.review_text: Dwarf Fortress is quite a hard game to get into but it's proving really interesting. The adventure mode is painful with being unable to heal or use most skills unless you use mods. The fortress mode is a really impressive colony sim and the world and history generation is really in depth. I'm looking forward to seeing the game progress and hope they update adventure mode to make it more seamless with fortress mode.

Bought it because i thought i could cook like in CDDA, but that is not a feature in adventure mode and modding this game is an absolute nightmare. Overall that's a pretty neat game, however if you're after survival elements then this game is not for you. 

I know this is still a work in progress, but i'm just gonna have to wait until they decide to do an overhaul in the survival aspect before i can actually play instead of testing different homebrew mods for 50 hours.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that certain items and byproducts like butchered creature parts and worn clothing accumulate as useless junk because there are not intuitive ways to dispose of or manage them.

citations.review_text: I've played this game long before it came to Steam. I've spent may hours playing this game. This game is a classic. That being said, the game needs a major overhaul. The user interface is terrible. It has a sharp learning curve if you never played this game before in part because the user interface. The graphics would be way better if they used something like Rimworld. When your fortress becomes large, it is difficult to manage and easy for it to fall into chaos when dwarves start going crazy.  Nothing has been fixed to utilize the trash created from killing creatures like cartilage, nervous system, scales and other stuff created when butchering a creature. The items are useless and not easy to dispose of.  You end up with a dump spot with hundreds of junk stuff that sits there until you reach magma and can finally toss it in the fire. I've never been able to use step ladders or harvest from trees. Dwarves will toss worn clothes all over the place and no one will ever pick it up or put it in a stockpile. The one person that is doing all the development of the game needs to hire a professional team and get this game fixed properly if he wants to make a high quality game.  The game has all kinds of half finished ideas that currently serve no purpose, like vials, extracts, forging coins, trapping vermin.  Little dead vermin whose corpses pile up everywhere like I don't see the point of junk like dead hamster in lizards in my stockpile that never decomposes or disappears, have to throw them into the massive dump spot with all the other junk, who has time clicking dump on every little tiny corpse when you managing a large fortress.

I was looking forward to playing Dwarf Fortress, but I was disappointed. I've been tracking it for several years, well before the Steam version, but put off for the text-based visuals, and what I assumed would be a challenging user experience. I assumed a graphical interface in Steam would be easier to use, and more visually appealing.

To be fair, that's true. The visuals are basic, but quite acceptable for a game of this type. My disappointment is the lack of quality of life, and the unrealised way the game's features seem to be expressed.

The interface is heavy on clicking and manual interaction. Particularly painful are the interfaces to remove furniture, redesign rooms and set up work orders - all of these are core and you'll be using them constantly. Doing so is painful, slow, highly repetitive and not-always intuitive.

I had read much of the game's much celebrated simulation aspects; lots of different materials, and properties, intricate granularity to creatures, and individual personalities and drivers. These are all there, but they seem meaningless when far-more core features of the game and user experience are absent. Materials seem to have little relevance in general, especially those without specific function like decorative stone or metal. The creature granularity feels like unnecessarily complexity for its own sake; it doesn't seem to add much (as entertaining as it is to read the very detailed accounts of how creatures were damaged in battle). And the core gameplay loop is so straightforward as to make most of the remaining variety and complexity seemingly pointless.

The game's community strapline is 'losing is fun'. Maybe that's because losing is all there is. But for those who don't have 10s of hours to waste for the simple sake of negating idleness, playing to lose and have fun seems like meagre pickings. I'd rather enjoy have fun playing, personally.

The game isn't irredeemable by any means. It's worth a play. And there's a solid base here. Bu…

claims.claim: Reviewers experience severe frame rate drops and performance struggles shortly after embarking, despite hardware usage remaining below capacity.

citations.review_text:
Awesome game that I’d recommend to almost anyone. However, it is extremely poorly optimized, and you can run into severe FPS issues almost immediately after embarking.

This does not appear to be caused by insufficient hardware, as my CPU, GPU, and RAM usage are frequently below 50% while the game is still struggling.

I've been waiting three and a half years for the promised full keyboard support. The UI is awful, with its worst areas comparable to the worst areas of pre-steam DF except now you *have* to use a mouse and can't even do basic things anymore like scroll with arrow keys or the page keys or even fuzzy search. Playing Steam DF for more than 30 minutes at a time causes an RSI flare-up that no other game I have ever played has, including other colony sims like Rimworld and Songs of Syx.

So many little things are just gone. Health screen, wound overview, civilian alerts (technically not but you need DFHack to access them). Not to even mention the bugs, some of which were years old pre-Steam. Its a shame because the performance improvements, worldgen speed, and the siege update are awesome.

A proper re-introduction of keyboard support has been a "top priority" and "in the works" and "coming soon" for literal YEARS, and now the new cope is "lua support might let DFHack fix it, maybe I guess". 

And no, the free version does not fix this. That is just the Steam version set to ASCII mode and still has the exact same UI.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a complex learning curve and can be beginner-hostile, requiring external guides like the wiki or video tutorials.

citations.review_text: A much more accessible version of Dwarf Fortress, for everyone who doesn't want to have to install a tileset themselves and run a few extra programs on the side. I still play with the wiki open, but such is Dwarf Fortress. Remember, Losing Is Fun!

I have had such a blast playing this game, and you will too after a few tutorials. I'll admit the game is a bit beginner hostile, but that should absolutely not stop you. If you get bored of base game or feel like some mechanics are a bit too unrewarding or obtuse, there's a million mods to simplify, adjust, and change the gameplay experience for you without sucking the fun out of it. The only criticism I have is that the dwarves, industrious and creative as they are, are also dumb as the rocks they mine, so I would also heavily recommend DFHack so you can take a bit more direct action in maintaining your forts

Now you may ask yourself "Well if I have to modify and change and cheat in the game is it even that fun?" and let me tell you, no amount of cheating will ever make this game "Too Easy", and that's why I recommend all of these bells and whistles. It's still a grind, but it's a relaxing grind that will suck you in for hours at a time.

Total newbie to Dwarf Fortress! Found it to be a really fun & addicting game, but requires some work/patience to learn. Don't send too many units on missions or the game can bug out!

The tutorial was nice to get me started but there's a lot to learn. Even after 100 hours I still spend time looking things up on the wiki!

I will say the only downside is encountering bugs, it's hard to tell if you are doing something wrong or it's just a quirk of the system. I've had a myriad of problems sending my units on missions. My armies of 100 dwarves with 2-3 animals per dwarf would be 'stuck' travelling and it took me forever to figure out that the game would hang on the missions because there were just too many squad members. Sending 1-3 squads has helped!

I'm also prone to wrist pain, so the repetitive clicking can be a bit much. Dwarfhack lets me multi-select which REALLY helped me out. There could be some quality of life improvements like shift clicking to multi-select items for trading. But having a workaround helps.

That said though this is a really wonderful game you can get lost in, I've enjoyed every minute playing! I built a giant damn to  create large farmlands under my frosty tundra home, while trading gems for dinosaurs with the local elves. Strike the earth!

This is a dwarf game. All craftsdwarfship is of the highest quality. It is encrusted with miasma clouds, tantrum spirals, and carp that will absolutely wreck your fisherdwarf's day. This object menaces with spikes of !!FUN!!, a simulation so deep you can track the emotional state of a single cat, and a learning curve shaped like a vertical cliff.

I've been playing Dwarf Fortress on and off for years, and I keep coming back. Not because I've "beaten" it — you don't beat Dwarf Fortress. You survive. Or more often, you don't. And that's the whole magic of it.

I've logged 800+ hours on just the Steam version, and probably couple thousand more before that on the old free-to-play versions, so... what else can I say? It's a great simulator game that lets you create custom worlds, set your own gameplay goals, and add whatever mods, tweaks, or cheats you like.

The learning curve is a bleep if you're just starting out, so I do recommend having the DFWiki on hand and/or watching a few YouTube tutorials if/when you get stuck. But once it all clicks for you, it's downright addicting. 
Just keep the game's first premise in mind - Losing is Fun! - and you'll be fine.

Just one caveat: If you're the kind of person who wants their game to have a well-defined plot and assigned side-quests and a main Big Bad Evil Guy that you defeat to "win", you're going to haaaaaaaaate this. The game world, plot(s), and victory conditions are all whatever you make of them, and there's no real ending unless your fort/party either chooses to retire or gets wiped out.

I tried playing dwarf fortress before the steam version and I understand it but it but never stuck with it.
With the steam release giving added mouse controls and a nice GUI I have sunk hours into this now and love it so much more. 
Added if you are new to this watch a video and know that you will need to look things up in the wiki there are a lot even I still do even with my 400+ hours.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the user interface has inconsistent menus and can be unintuitive or unhelpful for newer players.

citations.review_text:
The most frustratingly promising game I've ever played. I really, really want to like it, but it's still super unintuitive, even to a lover of Rimworld, Crusader Kings and Kenshi. and annoys *far* more often than it delights.

Today, I thought I'd give it another go as a Goblin adventurer. Was guided towards a temple. Found the person I needed to talk to and clicked to have my character path to somewhere near them. He jumped in the water and drowned. Very, very slowly, without me being able to do anything. Losing was not fun.

Even outside of gameplay and UI woes, everything, whether people, cities, civilisations or magical artefacts, ends up with the same formulaic, jarring and faintly ridiculous names, like "Squigglyfarms Siltbuckets", which makes it hard to tell one thing from another, especially when it's only translated *some* of the time.

This will probably end up as an incredible and at least somewhat accessible game (and I hope it does!), but not in this decade.
I wish the UI was more consistent, especially all the menus for selecting dwarves/creatures in different contexts.

Even though the game praises itself for being out for years, UI is less that help with newer players, pop screens that wont disable on every new world start and basic systems that are now broken( digging aquifers to build your base) broken but only discussion found is a new update that will no doubt break more of what was already in place to help the players navigate even a little, or even testing it before pushing something to make sure it does change core mechanics of the game like light aquifer mean light and no the whole map making it unplayable to want dig down. All of this  for a quick buck.
A little awkward to play at first but very fun once the UI is learned.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that embarking on a new world is a lottery due to the difficulty of reading the terrain map before settling.

citations.review_text:
One of the first times I played Dwarf Fortress after buying it, I clicked a random spot on the world map and embarked in the most beautiful location I've ever seen.

A waterfall split a massive cliff into several sections, and I turned each one into its own district of my town. There was a residential district, a market district with a tavern, a crafts district, and a citadel surrounded by sheer cliffs. Every district was connected by drawbridges spanning deep chasms, with a raging river far below. It was, without a doubt, the most memorable fortress I've ever built.

Then my hard drive died, and I lost the save.

For the last six months I've been generating new worlds and embarking over and over, hoping to find a place like that again. And you know what? It's almost impossible.

The embark map is incredibly hard to read. Every time you pick what looks like an interesting river or cliff, it's basically a lottery. You embark, realize the terrain is nothing like you expected, quit back to the main menu, and start all over again.

I even tried searching in Adventure Mode, but that has its own limitations. The most frustrating one is the fog of war, which makes exploring the world for a good embark site painfully slow.

So here's the thing: the day the developers add a way to preview the actual embark map before embarking, I'll finally be able to explore the world properly, find the perfect location, and really enjoy the game. On that day, I'll happily change my review and call Dwarf Fortress a 10/10.

But until then, it's a game that constantly frustrates me because of its awkward embark system, an almost useless world map, and the inability to disable the fog of war.
